traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous, with no perianth. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 264 Piperaceae: herbs or shrubs, upright or climbing; leaves usually alternate, entire, rarely opposite or whorled, stalked; stipules joined to the stalk, or none; flowers minute, in dense spikes (sometimes the spikes in umbels), with no perianth; stamens 2 to 6; ovary superior, of one cell with one ovule; fruit a small berry. One carpel is read from the one-celled, one-ovuled ovary (inferred).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203, family Piperaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203, family Piperaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.bract_form.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 205, 206, family Piperaceae: bract form scale; each tiny flower subtended by a small bract; read as "scale".

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203, family Piperaceae: flower symmetry actinomorphic (each with a peltate bract); read as "actinomorphic".

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add drupe (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 205, 206: 1-seeded berry or drupe.

traits.inflorescence.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add spadix (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 205, 206: spike or spadix with many tiny flowers.

traits.carpels.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family high 3: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203: 1 or 3-4. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.
